purpose: Authored source of truth for seal exclusions. Compiled into seal-tree.py and verify-tree.py by artifacts/instance/tools/gen-seal-rules.py; the compiled block is committed, and C-SEAL-001 fails if it is stale.
why_compiled: verify-tree.py travels. land.sh ships it alone inside a courier and runs it against a tree that carries neither this config nor any shared module, so the tool must be self-contained. Compiling the authored config into the tool keeps one source of truth without giving the tool a runtime dependency — and it means a courier can never supply its own permissive exclusion policy.
excluded_names_note: Matched at ANY depth. Version-control metadata and build artifacts legitimately appear anywhere in a tree.
excluded_suffixes_note: Directory-name suffixes, matched at any depth.
excluded_root_names_note: Matched ONLY at the tree root. Never move an entry from here to excluded_names: a name matched at any depth is a bypass, not an exclusion — a file can be hidden from the manifest by placing it in a directory of that name inside loopstrap_core.
serena_note: Dev-lane symbolic tooling. Serena writes memories and an LSP cache into .serena/ during ordinary use, so sealing it would report drift on every session. project.yml is committed anyway, so the setup is shared and reviewable while everything Serena writes stays untracked. Two declared holes in the seal is where this should stop.
never_excludable_note: A floor the generator refuses to cross. Excluding the kernel should be impossible, not merely visible in a diff.
